raw_title: When Herstory Goes Viral: Popular Resistance in the State-Platform Nexus in China
raw_abstract: This article examines the rise of herstory content on Douyin to explore how feminist resistance takes shape within China’s platform environment. Drawing on digital ethnography, we develop the concept of popular resistance, a form of platform-mediated resistance whose popularity serves both as a condition of political traction and as a mechanism of containment. To clarify this duality, we identify two dimensions: (a) popularity on the platform, driven by trends, aestheticization, and commodification; and (b) popularity within orthodoxy, shaped by state-sanctioned values that render certain forms of feminist expression politically permissible. Popular resistance retains a critical, if slippery, edge. It gives voice to gendered injustices while remaining entangled with the algorithmic, commercial, and political infrastructures that simultaneously enable and discipline it. We conclude by proposing popular resistance as a transferable analytic for understanding how political expression in the digital age gains visibility, negotiates power, and persists within the very systems that constrain it.

plain_summary_en: This paper studies When Herstory Goes Viral: Popular Resistance in the State-Platform Nexus in China. In plain terms, it asks what is happening, why it matters for public communication, and what evidence the authors use. The likely focus is The, Resistance, And, Popular. The abstract suggests a computational analysis approach, which makes the work useful for understanding how communication changes in everyday life.
